_readme: External points template. Copy to external_points_config.json (project root), fill in your paths and calibration, delete the '_example' line and run: python pipeline/step8_visualise3d/main_visualise_external_points.py. It holds everything that script needs, so config.json is not read. Relative paths are resolved against the folder this file is in.

inputs._readme: What main_visualise_external_points.py draws. Give either csv, or labels and / or fg_labels (leave the others null). csv = a points.csv (main_points3d.py), a tracks_3d.csv (main_tracks3d*.py) or any csv with frame, x, y, z columns (plus n_views and / or track); one with a track column is drawn as tracks, any other as points coloured by frame. labels = the detector's YOLO predictions, fg_labels = the boxes the factor graph inserted (<result>/reprojection/labels): each a folder with one sub-folder per camera, whose name contains the camera's name (or its 'match' string), holding one .txt per frame anywhere below it ('class xc yc w h [conf]', frame number = the digits ending the file name). A run folder with one model works as labels. They are pooled, shifted by each camera's frame_offset, and matched and triangulated with the tracking3d settings below. videos = a folder with one video (or folder of frames) per camera, named after it; only needed for the fruit, leaves and arena frame, which are found in the images (null = not drawn). link = labels only: also link the triangulated points into tracks (no factor graph). arena = draw the arena objects (needs videos). save = also save the plot to this .png (null = only show it). show = open the interactive window.

cameras._readme: Calibration (OpenCV conventions), as 'cameras' in config.example.json. One entry per camera; the name (or its optional 'match' string) is what the label sub-folders and videos are matched by. matrix = 3x3 intrinsics. distortions = k1 k2 p1 p2 k3 for model 'pinhole' (k1 k2 k3 k4 for 'fisheye'). rotation (Rodrigues vector, or a 3x3 matrix) and translation are WORLD -> CAMERA; translation is multiplied by t_scale. image_size = [width, height] the calibration was done at, also used to turn the normalised labels into pixels when no video is given. frame_offset is added to that camera's label frame numbers to synchronise the views (a csv is taken as already aligned). A csv must have been made with this calibration, or it will not line up with the cameras. Cameras left null are skipped.

tracking3d._readme: Used for labels only (a csv is drawn as it is). conf_threshold = minimum confidence of a predicted box (null = all). max_epipolar_px / max_reprojection_px = cross-camera matching gates, in undistorted pixels. static_radius_px / static_min_fraction = predictions at a spot the detector fires on in at least that fraction of a view's frames are removed as background clutter (null = keep them); factor-graph labels are never removed. link_max_distance (world units) / link_max_frame_gap / min_tracklet_frames = the linker used with link.

arena_plotting._readme: Fruit, leaves and arena frame, drawn when inputs.videos is given; the same settings as 'arena_plotting' in config.example.json, where each is described. Fits are cached in <output_dir>/external/<videos folder name>/3d/.
